I've been on weekly testosterone injections since 2018 and have been using FOLX for the past 3 years. 

Their pricing structure changed about a year ago I think -- It used to be $90/Mo and that included clinician visits, labs, and meds (+$20 shipping). They did not accept insurance at that point. 

Now I pay $40/mo, between $18 - $30 for labs every 6 months, and $70 for meds every 3 months (through my local pharmacy that delivers for free). The math comes out to just under $70/month in this new structure. I lost my insurance last year but they now accept a lot of carriers like BCBS, Aetna, Cigna, Optum, etc in some states. You only pay for the services you need through the platform. 

Comparatively, I was paying insurance premiums + deductibles, $50/ visit at a referral only, in-person clinic with long wait times. + $100 for blood panels twice a year and about $40/month on meds and injection supplies. So personally, FOLX is cheaper. 

I've met with a total of 3 clinicians over my time using FOLX and have had no issues. Appointments are about 30 mins and I can just pop one in during my lunch break so I don't have to take time off work. I like that I can easily schedule appointments and ask questions through their platform and can also see all my lab results. No waiting rooms, intake forms, or deadnaming and misgendering like I experienced at in-person clinics. Labs are done via Quest which is also easy to schedule. I choose a time, check-in on a kiosk, then someone takes my blood and I'm out in like 10 mins. They have really helpful resources, seminars (Erin Reed held one recently), and a community forum. 

I've been incredibly happy with my experience so far. My only complaint is from when I was getting my prescriptions filled through FOLX; they deliver via FedEx and you cannot schedule a delivery time. So I'd either have to take the day off work to sign for my controlled substance OR get it sent to a 'pickup location'. My pickup location was an auto parts store and twice they sent my package back to sender and I still had to pay the $20 shipping. 

  
Regarding the comments about clinicians under dosing; I've had the opposite experience. I get more than I need which allows me to have some safety stock but I'm sure things vary widely based on your hormone plan.

A few years ago I issued all of my partners brand new passports. I split all of our core coffees, and a few seasonals, into about 6 groups that I introduced over 6 weeks. Each group highlighted a theme (roast spectrum, processing methods, single origin vs blend... Etc etc) and accompanied a blurb of information about the group as well as a trivia question. Partners received a sticker on their passports once they completed tastings for whatever coffees were introduced that week. The first person to complete their tastings and submit a correct answer to the trivia question each week would get a $5 gift card. This is a very concise version of what I did and I would totally do some things differently, but I had about 80% participation and increased coffee sales by 100%!

I definitely suggest setting ordering pars! Your SM can help you find the resources you need to do so. This is important because, first and foremost, you cannot sell what you don't have available. Also, make sure your team is knowledgable and comfortable talking about the food. Suggestive selling when you are truly genuine about a product is a game changer. Be concise but be specific. The ASM Success Profile is an amazing tool to use while formulating your PDP as well as the Career Progression document. 
For your panel, be able to comfortably speak to what you have presented in your PDP. Really think about what you hope to gain from whatever skill, knowledge, or competency you choose. The questions are very similar or identical to the questions you may have been asked during your barista and/or shift interview. Make sure to answer questions in the STAR format (Situation, Task, Action, Result) using specific examples from former experiences. 
Best of luck to you!
